title: MV So I don't like RPG Maker 's event editor.

posts.author: Wrongful
posts.body:
It's very restrictive in general, especially for my project. My player character has different on-map abilities that can be used to get different responses from different events, so that's a number of different "event chains" even if all other conditions are the same, making for a long and layered event chains that are just tedious and compressed on MV's small event editor window. MZ doesn't fix this issue either. Maybe I'm just too used to scripting, but even for relatively simple events, it just feels impractical.
Is there
any
alternative to the default editor window for MV events? A plugin that lets you script events in a text editor instead? Some third-party editor? I understand that events in their raw .json format have a lot of numbers and are difficult to work with directly, but I'm open to any ideas or suggestions.
If there's absolutely no good alternative, I might end up making some hideous plugin myself for it.

It's kind of hard to tell what you're asking for, but… if scripting events in a text editor is the way you prefer to work, then you can totally do that. Make a .js file, fill it with functions for each event, and enable it as a plugin, and in the event editor, just add a single script call to call that function. If you want complicated functions to decide whether a page is active, you can add HIME_CustomPageConditions and then just do the same thing with your conditions (though you may run into issues where the event doesn't properly switch pages when the condition changes).
Personally, I'd recommend just using the event editor, at least for anything simple. But for more complicated mechanics, doing most of the work in a JavaScript file isn't that bad of a choice.

Actually, to say it's like the JS switch statement might be slightly misleading. It's probably a bit more like the Python match statement, in that the case values don't need to be constants but can in fact be expressions.
